title: The updater treats whatever the update channel returns as an authorized release, so redirecting the channel decides what every client installs
index_line: T-0088 · EXEC · update manifest + installer fetched and run without signature or certificate verification · cpp · corroborated
invariant_violated: The updater assumed that an update fetched from its configured update host is authentic because it came from that host. Nothing in the chain proved that: the manifest carried no signature and the installer's publisher was never checked, so control of the channel — not the vendor's signing key — decided what code every client would run.

mechanism.does: the client asks its configured update host for available versions and receives a manifest
the updater parses the XML manifest and reads the download URL and version it names
the installer is fetched from whatever host the manifest names — no pinned origin, no signature over the manifest
the downloaded installer's signer/certificate is never compared against the vendor's expected identity (the check that the fix adds)
the installer is written to disk and launched
the attacker's installer runs with the user's privileges, so a redirected update becomes code execution on every targeted client

source.http.request.value: the update check/download: the manifest and installer come from a URL the client trusts by configuration

guard.signature.value: the absent signature/certificate verification of manifest and installer (CWE-494)

delegate.tool.value: the updater as a delegate that runs whatever installer it fetched

sink.exec.shell.value: the launched installer executing with the user's privileges

preconditions.expr: the installed version predates 8.8.9 (WinGUp without certificate/signature verification)

check.spec: ls -l /usr/bin/notepad++ 2>/dev/null; reg query 'HKLM\\Software\\Notepad++' //v Version 2>/dev/null || printf 'check Help > About or the WinGUp exe version\n'

preconditions.expr: the client can reach its update channel and the channel can be controlled or redirected
the updater does not verify a signature over the manifest

success: the updater installs an installer whose publisher does not match the vendor
the update request is served by a host other than the configured one and the install still proceeds
failure_like: the updater rejects the manifest because its signature does not verify (8.8.9+ behaviour for the installer, 8.9.2+ for XMLDSig)
the installer's certificate is not the expected publisher
false_positive: an unsigned local build installed manually is not this bug — the vulnerable path is the automatic update check
a redirect to a CDN with a valid vendor-signed installer is normal update delivery

hazards: every self-updating desktop app, agent, and appliance: the update channel is an unauthenticated code path by construction
hosting compromise and traffic redirection are enough; the software's own code need not be vulnerable
detection is asymmetric: the install is legitimate-looking and the vendor may not see the redirected subset
non_transfers: updaters that verify a signature over both manifest and payload against a pinned key
updates delivered only through a package manager with its own repository signatures

provenance.author: VulnCheck
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2025-15556 (CWE-494): WinGUp downloaded update metadata and installers are not cryptographically verified; an attacker able to intercept or redirect update traffic causes the updater to download and execute an attacker-controlled installer with the user privileges

provenance.author: Notepad++ (Don Ho, incident advisory)
provenance.corroborates: vendor account of the resulting hijack: hosting-level compromise let actors redirect update traffic for targeted users to attacker-controlled manifests; WinGup was enhanced in v8.8.9 to verify both certificate and signature of the downloaded installer, the update XML is now XMLDSig-signed, and attackers specifically targeted the domain to exploit insufficient update verification controls
